name: עָכְרָן
summary: A man of Asher, known only as the father of Pagiel, Asher’s prince in the wilderness, who stood with Moses at the numbering, brought Asher’s offering on the eleventh day of the altar’s dedication, and led Asher’s host when the camps set out from Sinai (Num 1:13; 7:72; 10:26). The name is the root עכר, “stir up, trouble”, with the ending ־ָן; whether it means one troubled or one who troubles is not shown by any verse.

evidence.note: “Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Asher, Pagiel son of עָכְרָן.”
The prince of the sons of Asher, camped beside Dan.
On the eleventh day, the prince of the sons of Asher brings his offering (and 7:77).
The root’s verb: עֲכַרְתֶּם אֹתִי, “you have troubled me”.
The niphal, “my pain was stirred up”.

note: The ending ־ָן is the one in other names such as זִמְרָן and עֶבְרֹן; it may make a noun of the root (“trouble”) or an adjective of one marked by it. Nothing in the text says why he was so named; compare 1Ch 4:9, where Jabez is named for his mother’s pain.
